newsitem.title: UK: First Leisure shares fall on profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: First Leisure shares fall on profit outlook.

text.p: Shares in First Leisure Corp Plc were indicated lower on Tuesday after the company reported a fall in half-year profits and said trading in the second half was short of expectations.
The shares fell 18-1/2p to 317-1/2p by 0718 GMT in pre-market trade.
Pretax profit of 17.2 million stg compared with 18.1 million a year ago but was still at the top of the range of analysts forecasts.
But an interim dividend of 2.64p per share was below expectations of a 2.7-2.75p payout.
"The results were a bit disappointing," said one leisure analyst at a leading brokerage. "We will have to look at our estimates again."
The company said good weather in May had not helped its indoor businesses and trading in the first few weeks of the second half was slightly below expectations.
The group's bingo business also continued to struggle. Turnover improved by nine percent during the first half whilst comparable sales were down 25 percent.
First Leisure said in its results statement that Bingo was not yet showing signs of recovering and at current trading levels its performance would be similar to that seen in the first half.
